obligation: Provider notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the payment provider (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N44-45-R01)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data, including a fraud or common point of purchase notice from the provider
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). Clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation
notify: Payment provider's merchant risk or incident line (Bookkeeper or Owner)

obligation: Card brand compromise procedures, including forensic investigation (contractual)
citation: Payment brand operating rules, applied through the provider and its acquiring bank - not law
trigger: Provider or a card brand opens a compromise case
deadline: Per provider and brand instructions (brand rules not verified); a PCI Forensic Investigator may be required
notify: Provider; card brands through the provider
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow the provider's instructions; brand rules were not verified

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a credit or debit card number and any required security code, and an email address or user name with a password for an online account (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 additional days only if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)); the extension applies only to this notice
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email (501.171(4)(d))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for skimmed cards with security codes

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the store reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep at least 5 years, and provide to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (the worked example in P08 has about 72)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

obligation: Florida deemed compliance through a federal regulator's notice rules
trigger: Notice made under the rules of the covered entity's primary or functional federal regulator
deadline: Per that regulator's rules; a timely copy to the Department is deemed compliance with 501.171(3)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store has no primary or functional federal regulator with breach notice rules; follow 501.171 directly

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the store (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example the provider, the MSP, or the marketing freelancer) has a breach of a system it maintains for the store
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The store (Store Manager and Owner); the store then sends the notices under 501.171(3) and (4)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected customers reside (for example seasonal residents)

trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card data
notify: FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office

trigger: Suspected security incident, card compromise, or extortion
deadline: Prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event (unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information)
trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC via online form at ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store offers no credit and is not a financial institution under Part 314

trigger: Breach of unsecured protected health information by a covered entity
deadline: Individuals no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store has no pharmacy and is not a HIPAA covered entity

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines an incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope: critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard, or meeting a sector criterion regardless of size; the store is far below its SBA size standard

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store holds no federal contracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store holds no federal contracts
